title: Chakuli Pitha
steps: Soak rice and urad dal, grind into a smooth batter and ferment overnight.
Heat a tawa or pan, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thin round pancake. Cook on both sides with a little oil/ghee.
Serve hot with dalma, santula, coconut chutney, jaggery or milk.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday Odia rice-lentil pancake – softer and thicker than dosa.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A staple breakfast across Odisha households.

title: Pakhala Bhata
steps: Soak cooked rice in water overnight to ferment lightly (basi pakhala).
In the morning, mix with salt, crushed green chilli and cumin. Add curd for dahi pakhala if preferred.
Serve cool with badi chura, roasted vegetables, lemon and any side.

fullIngredients.name: Curd (optional for dahi pakhala), green chilli, cumin, salt
Sides: badi chura, roasted vegetables, saga bhaja

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic cooling summer dish of Odisha – probiotic and hydrating.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Traditionally served in kansa (bell-metal) utensils.

title: Dahibara Aloodum
steps: Make soft urad dal vadas (bara), soak in water, then in spiced yogurt.
Prepare a spicy potato curry (aloodum) with mustard oil and local spices.
Serve the dahi bara topped with aloodum, sev, onion and coriander.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Popular street and breakfast combination in Cuttack and across Odisha.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The contrast of cool yogurt bara and hot spicy aloodum is signature.

title: Dalma
steps: Pressure-cook dal and chopped vegetables together with turmeric and salt till soft.
Temper pancha phutana, cumin and dry red chilli in ghee or oil. Add to the dalma along with grated coconut.
Simmer briefly. Serve with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Mixed vegetables (pumpkin, raw banana, brinjal, papaya, drumstick)
Pancha phutana, cumin, dry red chilli, grated coconut, ghee

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The soul of Odia cuisine – lentils and vegetables cooked together.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Temple (Jagannath) versions are strictly satvik (no onion/garlic).

title: Machha Besara
steps: Grind mustard seeds with garlic, green chilli and turmeric into a paste.
Marinate fish lightly. Heat mustard oil, add the paste and cook briefly.
Add fish and a little water. Simmer gently till cooked. Do not over-stir.
Serve with steamed rice.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard seeds, garlic, green chilli, turmeric

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic Odia mustard-based fish curry – pungent and flavourful.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mustard oil and freshly ground mustard are essential.

title: Santula
steps: Boil or steam the chopped vegetables with turmeric and salt till tender but not mushy.
Temper pancha phutana and dry red chilli in oil. Pour over the vegetables and mix gently.
Serve as a light dry or semi-dry side with rice and dalma.

fullIngredients.name: Mixed seasonal vegetables (potato, brinjal, pumpkin, beans, etc.)
Pancha phutana, dry red chilli, turmeric, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple, lightly tempered mixed vegetable dish – everyday Odia home cooking.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Highlights seasonal produce with minimal spices.

title: Chhena Poda
steps: Knead fresh chhena with sugar, cardamom and a little semolina until smooth. Mix in nuts and raisins.
Grease a baking tin or traditional vessel with ghee. Pour the mixture and bake in a moderate oven or traditional coal oven till the top is caramelised and the centre is set.
Cool, slice and serve.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Literally 'burnt cheese' – Odisha's signature baked dessert.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The caramelised crust is the hallmark of a good chhena poda.

title: Machha Jhola
steps: Lightly fry fish with turmeric. Set aside.
Make a gravy with onion, tomato, ginger-garlic and spices in mustard oil.
Add the fish and simmer in a light gravy. Garnish with coriander.
Serve with rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday light fish curry of Odia homes.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Less rich than mustard-based besara versions.

title: Bara (Urad Dal Vada)
steps: Soak urad dal, grind to a fluffy batter with green chilli, ginger and cumin. Add salt.
Shape into round vadas with a hole and deep-fry till golden.
Serve hot with ghugni, chutney or as part of dahibara.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Essential component of dahibara aloodum and also eaten plain.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Soft and airy texture comes from well-aerated batter.

title: Enduri Pitha
steps: Prepare a fermented rice-urad batter. Make a sweet coconut-jaggery filling.
Spread batter on a turmeric leaf, place filling, fold the leaf and steam.
Serve warm. The turmeric leaf imparts a unique aroma.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Special pitha made for Prathamastami festival.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Steamed in turmeric leaves for distinctive fragrance.

title: Saga Bhaja (Greens Stir-fry)
steps: Heat mustard oil, add crushed garlic and dry red chilli.
Add washed greens and salt. Stir-fry on high heat till just wilted.
Serve as a dry side with rice and dalma or pakhala.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard oil, garlic, dry red chilli, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday green side – Odisha has a rich variety of local saga.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Quick cooking preserves colour and nutrients.

title: Mansha Tarkari (Mutton Curry)
steps: Marinate mutton with turmeric and salt. Brown with onions and whole spices in mustard oil.
Add ginger-garlic, potatoes and spices. Add water and slow-cook till tender.
Serve with rice or roti.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard oil or ghee, turmeric, garam masala

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Odia mutton curry is moderately spiced and often includes potatoes.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Special-occasion dish in many households.
